# Getting Started

Mayon runs as a SvelteKit SPA backed by a Mayon server with Postgres, all orchestrated by Docker Compose.

## Docker (primary)

Pull and run with Docker Compose:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bendlikeabamboo/mayon.git
cd mayon
docker compose up
```

Open `http://localhost:8080` in your browser. Data is stored in Postgres inside the `pg-data` docker volume and persists across restarts.

## Development

For active development, bring up the entire stack (web + server + Postgres) in Docker:

```bash
pnpm dev   # all-Docker dev stack: web HMR on :5173 + server + Postgres
```

Web changes hot-reload via Vite; the dev container proxies `/api` requests to
the Dockerized server.

## First run

When you open Mayon for the first time the server boots, connects to Postgres, and runs migrations automatically. Look for the status pill in the header:

- **DB status pill** — reads "DB ready" once the database is up. The pill's status area also shows a separate "Runtime: …" line telling you where the database is running, along with the result of the boot self-check. In development builds that self-check writes, reads, and deletes a test row to confirm the database is functional.

You can also confirm storage is working by switching the theme with the sun/moon icon in the header and reloading the tab — the theme persists.

If the server is unreachable, Mayon shows a full-screen message: "Cannot reach the Mayon server." The screen includes a `docker compose up` hint and a Retry button. Start the stack with `docker compose up`, then click Retry (or simply wait — Mayon keeps checking for the server and recovers on its own).

## The home dashboard

After boot you land on the home screen, not directly inside a chat. The dashboard greets you and keeps your ongoing work one click away: a **Continue learning** card picks up your most recently touched conversation, and the page also lists your **Recent chats**, **In-progress labs**, and **Recent quizzes** as they accumulate. Below the greeting, a starter prompt ("Explore a new topic") is available: clicking it starts a fresh chat and sends an opening message that asks what you are curious about.

One more stop worth making before your first conversation: open **Settings** and find the **Learner profile** section. There you set your default knowledge level and preferred teaching mode, and Mayon pre-fills that context into each new chat's learning brief, so replies start at the right level.

## Start your first conversation

The fastest way in is the starter prompt on the home dashboard: click **Explore a new topic** and Mayon opens a new chat and sends the opening message for you. You can also start from scratch — open the chat list, click **New chat**, and either fill in a short learning brief (what you want to learn and at what level) or skip it and just start chatting. Type a message in the composer and the assistant replies right in the chat, with your topic saved automatically. When you're ready to go deeper, the [chat and branching tutorial](chat-and-branching.qmd) shows how to branch a conversation and explore alternative replies.
